nodes.description: GJB1 mutations cause loss of function of connexin-32, which forms reflexive gap-junction channels across the non-compact myelin of the paranodes and Schmidt-Lanterman incisures, shortening the radial diffusion pathway between the Schwann-cell body and the adaxonal cytoplasm. nodes.description: The shared terminal node of the demyelinating compartment. Primary Schwann-cell and myelin defects (PMP22 dosage, MPZ misfolding, connexin-32 gap-junction failure) converge on segmental demyelination and repeated remyelination (onion-bulb formation), which over time produces length-dependent secondary axonal degeneration. It is this secondary axonal loss, affecting the longest motor and sensory fibers first, that determines the progressive clinical deficit shared with the axonal compartment.

nodes.description: EGR2, also called Krox20, is a Cys2His2 zinc-finger protein that binds DNA in a sequence-specific manner and acts as a transcription factor, and stable expression of its mouse orthologue is specifically associated with the onset of peripheral myelination. Egr2-null mice arrest Schwann-cell differentiation at an early stage, and missense mutations in the conserved functional domains of human EGR2 were found in congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy and in a CMT1 family. The lesion is therefore a failure of the transcriptional programme that drives a Schwann cell into the myelinating state, rather than a defect in a myelin structural protein.

nodes.description: FBLN5 encodes fibulin-5, a widely expressed extracellular matrix constituent with an essential role in elastic fibre assembly; loss-of-function alleles cause cutis laxa. Heterozygous missense variants segregate with demyelinating CMT, and the same variant class produces concurrent pathology in eye and skin, which is why FBLN5 families combine neuropathy with macular degeneration and hyperextensible skin. The step from an elastic-fibre defect to Schwann-cell demyelination is not established by the cited work, and is recorded here as an unexplained gap rather than asserted.

nodes.description: LITAF, also called SIMPLE, is a small integral membrane protein of the late endosome and lysosome, and autosomal dominant mutations in it cause CMT1C. Primary fibroblasts from two CMT1C patients carrying different pathogenic LITAF variants show vacuolation and enlargement of late endosomes and lysosomes, and the same morphology follows knocking LITAF out of control fibroblasts, which is consistent with loss of function. The same phenotype occurs in CMT4J fibroblasts carrying FIG4 variants and is rescued in both by a small-molecule activator of the lysosomal channel TRPML1, so LITAF and FIG4 appear to act on one endolysosomal pathway. This lesion is unlike the other CMT1 subtypes modeled here. LITAF is widely expressed, and its transcript level in sciatic nerve is not altered during development or in response to nerve injury, which the founding report calls a stark contrast to the other known CMT1 genes.

evidence.reference_title: NEFL / Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (Definitive)
evidence.snippet: NEFL | HGNC:7739 | Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease | MONDO:0015626 | AD | Definitive

nodes.description: NEFL encodes neurofilament light protein, one of five proteins that co-assemble to form neurofilaments, and its variants are classified as demyelinating (CMT1F), axonal (CMT2E) or dominant intermediate (DI-CMTG) according to electrodiagnostic findings. Many reports find that missense mutations in NEFL disrupt neurofilament assembly in cultured cells. How that produces the absence of neurofilaments from axons is less settled: the review collating the published cases calls it less clear, and says only that it seems likely to involve defective assembly and/or transport, which is why this node is named for both and asserts neither alone. The same review argues that the CMT1F, CMT2E and DI-CMTG classification reflects variable presentation rather than different mechanisms, and that the process is most likely primarily axonal in all cases; the node is placed in this entry because sural nerve biopsies in NEFL-related CMT show onion bulbs or thin myelin sheaths in two-thirds of cases alongside uniform loss of large myelinated fibres.

nodes.description: The most common cause of CMT (CMT1A) is a 1.4 Mb tandem duplication of chromosome 17p11.2 containing the peripheral myelin protein 22 (PMP22) gene. PMP22 overexpression destabilizes compact myelin and disrupts the structural organization of the myelin sheath, causing dysmyelination, demyelination, and characteristic onion-bulb formation from repeated Schwann-cell remyelination attempts. Slowed nerve conduction follows, and chronic secondary axonal loss eventually drives the clinical phenotype.
